topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic frames the lecture within the cancer course and states what students should learn.

topics.label: Genetic origins and determinants of cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain cancer as an evolutionary process whose development depends on mutation acquisition and the biological context of affected cells.

topics.label: Environmental cancer risk and the evidence for it
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how environmental contributions to cancer risk can be recognized and interpreted against the background of chance and inherited susceptibility.

topics.label: Infectious agents in cancer development
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how infection can drive carcinogenesis, using Burkitt lymphoma to develop the interaction between pathogens and cancer-producing cellular changes.

topics.label: Environmental mutagens and mechanisms of DNA damage
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace how environmental exposures produce DNA damage that can become cancer-associated mutations.

topics.label: Tumour initiation and promotion
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish why mutational initiation may require a subsequent growth-promoting environment before tumours develop.

topics.label: Tissue susceptibility and recap of carcinogenic mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics conclude the mechanistic discussion by emphasizing that the consequences of carcinogen exposure depend on the biological context of the affected tissue.

topics.label: Tracing carcinogen exposure in human cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how evidence collected from people can connect cancer development to prior carcinogen exposure.

topics.label: Experimental carcinogenicity testing and its limitations
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics assess how controlled experimental tests detect carcinogenic potential and why their results may not fully predict human cancer risk.

topics.label: Closing summary and risk–benefit perspective
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic closes the lecture by summarizing its conclusions and placing cancer-risk decisions in a risk–benefit framework.
